headline: All seven majors sit below their 200-day line while BTC ETF desks post a fifth straight day of net buying
paragraphs: Start with structure, because it's uniform today: BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, BNB, DOGE and ADA are all below their 200-day moving average, none show a golden cross, and every one of them is sitting well off its 12-month high (BTC -47.9%, ETH -60.1%, SOL -69.2%, XRP -68.1%, BNB -53.7%, DOGE -75.4%, ADA -79.2%). That's a market still working off a long drawdown even though six of the seven closed green on the day. BTC's 1.17% move and RSI of 55.3 with MACD above signal reads as a short-term uptick sitting inside a longer downtrend, not a trend reversal by itself.

Momentum against trend is where the interesting splits show up. ADA has an RSI of 69.3, MACD above signal, up 23.41% over seven days and 39.24% over thirty, yet it's still 79.2% off its high, the widest gap between short-term acceleration and long-term damage on this board. XRP sits at the other extreme: RSI 41, MACD below signal, down 2.06% over the week, the weakest momentum reading here even though its drawdown (-68.1%) is less severe than ADA's. ETH is its own small divergence today: price up 1.06% but MACD still below signal, momentum resting even as the tape ticks up.

Positioning tells a two-speed story. Funding is cheap on BTC (2.7% annualized), slightly negative on ETH (-0.4%), and modest on XRP (3.8%), meaning longs there aren't paying much to hold the bet. SOL and DOGE are a different animal at 11% annualized funding each, with long/short ratios stretched to 2.55 and 4.65 respectively, XRP's ratio also runs hot at 3.53. Liquidations show the squeeze landing unevenly: SOL saw $2.29M in short liquidations against just $345,763 in longs over 24 hours, consistent with its 5.02% day catching short positioning offside. BTC ran the other way, with longs taking $781,061 in liquidations against $372,521 for shorts, on a day BTC was actually up, a reminder that a green tape doesn't spare leveraged longs on the wrong side of a wick.

On flows, the BTC spot ETF took in $101.7M on 07 Aug, capping a run where all five of the last sessions leaned the same direction for a combined $865.3M. ETH ETF added $49.6M on the same date, with four of the last five sessions in the same direction for $243.7M over that window, a slightly less clean streak. The whale ledger complicates the picture: the aggregate 24-hour print shows $30.3M net moving onto exchanges, but that's almost entirely an ETH story, $77.5M deposited with zero recorded outflow against it, while BTC actually saw $47.2M net leave exchanges over the same window. Zoom out to the four-period weekly whale series (-$279.9M, +$380.9M, +$1,108.3M, +$297.1M) and three of the last four windows favor coins leaving exchanges, the more accumulative posture, even as today's single print points the other way for ETH. Stablecoin float, at $306.2B, has slipped 0.75% over the last 30 days, so the dry powder sitting on the sidelines is a touch smaller, not building.

Sentiment is the foil here. Fear & Greed reads 30, labeled Fear, sitting near the top of its own 30-day range of 22 to 33. That's a crowd still describing itself as scared on the same day the BTC ETF posts its fifth consecutive net-positive session and most majors trade green. When the mood gauge and the money disagree this plainly, the disagreement itself is the notable thing, not a signal to resolve one way or the other.

Worth watching from here: whether any major reclaims its 200-day line, whether the BTC ETF same-direction streak breaks, whether SOL and DOGE funding cools off its current 11% annualized reading, and whether the weekly whale series turns uniformly negative rather than the mixed pattern it shows now.
